reads.title: Why the same two moves
reads.body:
You made one transfer in GW10, Schade for Rogers, so the two players the model wanted out are still here. Their problem has not changed: minutes. The model expects about 71 minutes a game from Calafiori and about 43 from Szoboszlai. Szoboszlai scored 7 in GW10, which lifted his expected minutes from 32, but he is still the lowest in your squad.

Gabriel projects 31.0 points over GW11 to GW16, 9.0 more than Calafiori over the same games, with a full 90 and 9.1 defensive contributions per 90. Calafiori is in 80% of teams near your rank, but our template rule only keeps a player like that when the alternative is under 2 points better over six gameweeks. Over the next four alone Gabriel projects 6.0 more and is in 14.5% of teams near your rank, which is the aggressive case in our risk framework.

Tavernier projects 31.9 over the six weeks, the most of any midfielder, and he is already in 61% of teams near your rank. Szoboszlai projects 13.6.

The closest alternative is Hill instead of Gabriel: 0.3 points behind, owned by 3% near your rank, and it leaves £2.5m in the bank instead of nothing. That gap is inside the model's error, so either is a sound move. The call keeps Gabriel because he is the model's pick and the money Hill frees up does not buy a better move next week (see the template story). Rolling both transfers gives up about 14 projected points.

reads.title: How last week's advice did
reads.body:
These are facts from the prediction log, scored after GW10 was final.

The two recommended moves would have lost 2 points in GW10: Gabriel scored 8 to Calafiori's 6, and Tavernier scored 3 to Szoboszlai's 7. The model had projected a 5.0 point gain for that week. One week out of six says little about the plan, which is why it is still the call.

The captain was the costlier miss. The edition overrode the model's pick, Gabriel, for Haaland, under our rule to follow a captain that 70% or more of rivals pick unless the alternative projects 1.5 or more better. Haaland scored 2 and Gabriel 8, so the override cost 6 points. Barry, in your eleven, scored 16. The rule protects against Haaland hauling while you do not have the armband on him, and one blank does not prove it wrong, but the backtest is set to test it once a few more weeks are logged.

The model missed by 1.9 points a player on average across 363 players, and was too low by 0.3 on balance. It gave hauls of 10 or more a 1.5% chance on average; 4.2% of players hauled. That is the known bias toward flat projections. Holding the Free Hit was right: its eleven scored 62 against 68.

reads.title: Two template questions that can wait
reads.body:
After the call, the model's best eleven is a 5-3-2 with Palmer and Calvert-Lewin on the bench. Palmer projects 4.0 at home to Leeds, against 4.6 for De Cuyper, the fifth defender, and 4.8 for Barry. He is in 61% of teams near your rank, so benching him is a small risk against those managers. The gap is 0.6 points, so playing Palmer over De Cuyper is a fair choice if you prefer to match the field.

Jackson is the biggest template player you do not own: 77% of the sampled top 10k and 70% of teams near your rank. Over GW11 to GW16 the model projects him at 29.0, against 25.8 for Calvert-Lewin. That 3.2 point gap is not enough for a -4 this week. Even as a free transfer in GW12, his lead over GW12 to GW16 is about 2.3.

He costs £7.2m and Calvert-Lewin sells for £6.0m, so he needs £1.2m more. Palmer is the natural funding sale if you want him in GW12: Palmer projects 24.1 over the six weeks, the least of your five most expensive players. Calvert-Lewin's price is drifting down (34% of the way to a fall), so it is worth watching but not worth a hit.

reads.title: Why the Free Hit still waits
reads.body:
Your first Free Hit expires at the GW19 deadline, 1 Jan 18:30 UK. Every gameweek before then has all ten fixtures, so the chip is about fixtures and rotation cover, not rescuing a blank.

The planner now projects Free Hit gains of 4.2 to 7.8 points a week from GW11 to GW19. GW14 is still the tallest bar at 7.8, but GW19 (7.2) and GW18 (7.1) are within the model's error of it, and they fall in the festive run: deadlines on 26 Dec, 29 Dec and 1 Jan. That is when rotation is hardest to call and a Free Hit does the most to cover it. Nothing this week changes the plan.

figure.title: Projected Free Hit gain by gameweek

data_room.title: The transfer search, in full
data_room.body:
## Method

The planner scores a squad by the best eleven it can field each week from GW11 to GW16, with the captain counted twice, bench points at 10% and each later week weighted 8% less. A plan's gain is that score minus the score of making no transfers, minus 4 for each transfer beyond your two free ones. It searched every one and two transfer plan against the best projected players in each position, then extended the strongest with a third. Only legal squads count: three per club, within your £2.4m bank and your selling prices.

## The numbers

| Plan | Gain, 6 GWs | Hit | Bank after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calafiori, Szoboszlai → Gabriel, Tavernier | +14.1 | 0 | £0.0m |
| Calafiori, Szoboszlai → Hill, Tavernier | +13.8 | 0 | £2.5m |
| Calafiori, King → Hill, Tavernier | +13.3 | 0 | £1.3m |
| Calafiori, Szoboszlai, King → Hill, Tavernier, Mbeumo | +12.6 | -4 | £0.1m |
| Calafiori, Palmer → Gabriel, Tavernier | +12.6 | 0 | £3.0m |
| Szoboszlai → Tavernier, roll one | +8.2 | 0 | £2.4m |

Gains are after any hit.

## Alternatives considered

The best -4 plan lands 1.5 below the call, so it fails the rule that a hit must beat the best free plan by 2 points. The Hill version is 0.3 behind, which this model cannot separate from the call; it trades Gabriel's 15% ownership near your rank for Hill's 3% and keeps £2.5m. Selling Palmer instead of Szoboszlai projects 1.5 less.

## How confident we are

Fairly. Most of the gain comes from Szoboszlai's minutes, 43 a game against Tavernier's 87, and minutes are the model's weakest input. The GW10 result, -2 for the same moves, is one week and does not change that. The call spends the whole bank: Gabriel is 23% and Tavernier 28% of the way to a rise, so neither is likely to move tonight, but if either does the plan no longer fits. The model cannot see transfers made since the GW10 deadline, so check your squad before you confirm.

data_room.title: When to play your first Free Hit
data_room.intro: Your first Free Hit expires at the GW19 deadline (1 Jan, 18:30 UK). There are no blank gameweeks before then, so its value comes from fixtures and rotation.
data_room.bottom_line: Still GW18 or GW19. Decide on 26 Dec, with real team news.
data_room.body:
## Why not GW14, the tallest bar

GW14 projects 7.8 against 7.1 for GW18 and 7.2 for GW19. Those gaps are under a point, less than this model can tell apart. Playing it early also leaves nothing in hand for the festive run, when GW17, GW18 and GW19 land within seven days (deadlines 26 Dec, 29 Dec and 1 Jan).

## Why GW18 first

GW18 and GW19 are a tie on the numbers. GW18 comes after the Boxing Day games, so you see who was rested, and it keeps GW19 as a fallback. Waiting for GW19 leaves no second chance before the chip expires.

## How this was worked out

For each gameweek, the planner builds the best eleven your £101.6m budget allows, keeping money back for a cheap bench, and compares it with the best eleven from your current squad. The captain counts double in both. Projections come from the v0 model.
data_room.confidence: Not very, and that is why the call is to wait. The v0 model has no rotation model yet, which matters most in the festive weeks. Treat any gap under 1 point as a tie. Play it early only if three or more starters are out in the same week.
